difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism stimulus (A or B; ¬A; ∴ B) with distractors that share legal subject matter but use modus ponens or invalid forms, requiring students to formalize the structure.
stimulus: The defendant either acted in self-defense or committed an unprovoked assault. The evidence conclusively rules out self-defense. Therefore, the defendant committed an unprovoked assault.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The soil sample contains either limestone or granite. Laboratory analysis has confirmed that the sample contains no limestone. Therefore, the sample contains granite.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the reactor core overheats, a meltdown will occur. The reactor core has overheated. Therefore, a meltdown will occur.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Most treaties either create obligations or confer rights. This treaty creates obligations. Therefore, it probably does not confer rights.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The suspect could not have committed the robbery, since the robbery required physical strength and the suspect lacks physical strength.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Either the painting is a forgery or it was produced before 1800. Experts believe it was produced before 1800. Therefore, it is not a forgery.

explanations.correct: The stimulus is a disjunctive syllogism: A or B; ¬A; ∴ B. Choice A matches exactly — either limestone or granite; no limestone; therefore granite. Both premises and conclusion have the same form.
explanations.A: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism: A or B; ¬A; ∴ B — identical structure to the stimulus.
explanations.B: Trap: modus ponens (if A then B; A; ∴ B). Valid but a different logical form from the stimulus.
explanations.C: Trap: same-topic distractor using 'most' (a probabilistic quantifier) rather than an exhaustive disjunction, and the conclusion does not follow with certainty.
explanations.D: Trap: modus tollens or reductio structure (B requires A; ¬A; ∴ ¬B). Different form and no explicit disjunction.
explanations.E: Trap: inverts the disjunctive syllogism — the surviving disjunct is affirmed (belief in B), and the conclusion denies A. This treats disjunction as exclusive and reasons backward, which is invalid.

difficultyReason: Contrapositive stimulus (A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A) with distractors using the same medical domain or affirming the consequent, requiring students to distinguish modus tollens from modus ponens.
stimulus: Any patient who undergoes the surgical procedure will require post-operative physical therapy. This patient did not undergo post-operative physical therapy. Therefore, this patient did not undergo the surgical procedure.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every licensed architect must pass the national examination. Sonja has passed the national examination. Therefore, Sonja is a licensed architect.

choices.label: B
choices.text: All certified organic farms must rotate their crops annually. The Greenfield farm did not rotate its crops this year. Therefore, the Greenfield farm is not a certified organic farm.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If a language has tonal phonemes, its speakers must distinguish pitch carefully. Mandarin speakers distinguish pitch carefully. Therefore, Mandarin is a tonal language.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Whenever inflation rises sharply, central banks raise interest rates. The central bank has raised interest rates. Therefore, inflation has risen sharply.

choices.label: E
choices.text: A patient requires physical therapy only if the injury is severe. This patient's injury is severe. Therefore, this patient requires physical therapy.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A (modus tollens / contrapositive). Choice B: All certified organic farms → rotate crops; Greenfield did not rotate; ∴ Greenfield is not certified organic. Perfect structural match.
explanations.A: Trap: affirms the consequent (All A → B; B; ∴ A). Invalid form that inverts the conditional direction.
explanations.B: Correct. Modus tollens — universal conditional with denial of consequent yielding denial of antecedent.
explanations.C: Trap: same as A — affirms the consequent. Uses linguistics domain to disguise the form.
explanations.D: Trap: same form as A and C — affirms the consequent. Economics domain disguises the structural error.
explanations.E: Trap: same-topic (physical therapy) distractor using modus ponens (A → B; A; ∴ B), not modus tollens.

difficultyReason: Conditional chain (A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C) stimulus in ethics domain; distractors break the chain at different points or reverse a conditional, requiring careful tracking of three steps.
stimulus: Whenever a corporation knowingly deceives consumers, it violates its ethical obligations. Any company that violates its ethical obligations should be subject to regulatory oversight. NovaChem knowingly deceived consumers. Therefore, NovaChem should be subject to regulatory oversight.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If a river floods its banks, downstream farmland is damaged. If farmland is damaged, crop yields decline. The Arno River flooded its banks. Therefore, crop yields along the Arno will decline.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Companies that pollute waterways face heavy fines. NovaChem faces heavy fines. Therefore, NovaChem has polluted a waterway.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Any business that overcharges customers should be audited. Businesses that are audited often improve their practices. Dalton Co. overcharged customers. Therefore, Dalton Co. will probably improve its practices.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Regulatory oversight is imposed on companies that violate consumer-protection statutes. Companies subject to oversight must file quarterly reports. Therefore, companies that violate consumer-protection statutes must file quarterly reports.

choices.label: E
choices.text: When athletes use banned substances, they violate sporting rules. Violating sporting rules results in disqualification. Therefore, athletes who use banned substances face disqualification.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; A (particular); ∴ C (particular). Choice A: floods → farmland damaged; farmland damaged → yields decline; Arno flooded (particular); ∴ yields decline (particular). Three-step chain applied to a specific case — exact match.
explanations.A: Correct. Conditional chain with a specific instantiation, mirroring the stimulus precisely.
explanations.B: Trap: affirms the consequent (All polluters → fines; fines; ∴ polluter). Invalid form.
explanations.C: Trap: 'often improve' introduces probability ('probably'), shifting conclusion strength from certainty to likelihood — strength-shift trap.
explanations.D: Trap: correct conditional chain but lacks a particular instantiation; the conclusion is a universal generalization, not a particular case. Same-topic distractor.
explanations.E: Trap: valid conditional chain (A → B; B → C; ∴ A → C) but stays at the universal level — no specific athlete is named. Premise count and conclusion type differ.

difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular (All A are B; x is A; ∴ x is B) stimulus in linguistics domain; distractors use the same universal premise structure but apply it invalidly or shift to probabilistic language.
stimulus: All languages classified as ergative-absolutive assign the same grammatical case to the subjects of intransitive verbs and the objects of transitive verbs. Basque is classified as an ergative-absolutive language. Therefore, Basque assigns the same grammatical case to the subjects of intransitive verbs and the objects of transitive verbs.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: Every element in the halogen group reacts readily with alkali metals to form salts. Chlorine is an element in the halogen group. Therefore, chlorine reacts readily with alkali metals to form salts.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Most Romance languages derive the majority of their vocabulary from Latin. Portuguese is a Romance language. Therefore, Portuguese probably derives the majority of its vocabulary from Latin.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Languages with complex morphology are rarely adopted as lingua francas. Swahili has relatively simple morphology. Therefore, Swahili may serve as a lingua franca.

choices.label: D
choices.text: All endangered languages lack government protection. Ubykh lacks government protection. Therefore, Ubykh is an endangered language.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Some tonal languages are found in sub-Saharan Africa. Yoruba is a tonal language. Therefore, Yoruba is probably found in sub-Saharan Africa.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: All A are B; x is A; ∴ x is B — a valid universal instantiation. Choice A matches: All halogens react with alkali metals; chlorine is a halogen; ∴ chlorine reacts. Same form, certain conclusion.
explanations.A: Correct. Universal-to-particular instantiation with a certain conclusion.
explanations.B: Trap: strength-shift — uses 'most' (not 'all') in the first premise, so the conclusion is 'probably' rather than certain. Structural mismatch.
explanations.C: Trap: uses a negative universal ('rarely') and draws a permissive conclusion ('may'), neither matching the affirmative universal nor the certain conclusion of the stimulus.
explanations.D: Trap: affirms the consequent — All A → B; x has B; ∴ x is A. Invalid form despite the universal premise.
explanations.E: Trap: 'some' in the first premise and 'probably' in the conclusion — both quantifier and strength differ from the stimulus.

difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism in economic policy domain; distractors include one that affirms a disjunct (invalid) and one that uses a biconditional disguised as a disjunction.
stimulus: The budget shortfall must be addressed either by raising taxes or by cutting public services. The legislature has decided that taxes will not be raised. Therefore, public services will be cut.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The vaccine trial will be conducted either in the spring or in the autumn. Funding constraints have ruled out a spring trial. Therefore, the trial will be conducted in the autumn.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Either the new highway reduces commute times or it increases suburban sprawl. The highway will increase suburban sprawl. Therefore, commute times will not be reduced.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the central bank cuts interest rates, consumer borrowing will increase. The central bank has cut interest rates. Therefore, consumer borrowing will increase.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Economists agree that growth requires either investment or consumption. Investment has increased this quarter. Therefore, growth will occur this quarter.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The government can reduce the deficit only by raising taxes. Since raising taxes is politically infeasible, the deficit will not be reduced.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; ¬A; ∴ B. Choice A: spring or autumn; ¬spring; ∴ autumn. Identical disjunctive syllogism structure.
explanations.A: Correct. Disjunctive syllogism — exclusive options, one eliminated, the other concluded.
explanations.B: Trap: affirms one disjunct (sprawl increases) and then denies the other, treating the disjunction as exclusive and reasoning backward — invalid form.
explanations.C: Trap: modus ponens (if A then B; A; ∴ B). Valid but structurally different — no disjunction.
explanations.D: Trap: affirms one disjunct (investment) to conclude the overall goal (growth) — does not eliminate a disjunct. Same economic domain is a surface lure.
explanations.E: Trap: uses 'only if' (biconditional or necessary condition), not a disjunction. The form is A only if B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A (modus tollens), not disjunctive syllogism.

difficultyReason: Modus tollens in history domain; distractors include modus ponens with similar historical content and an invalid contrapositive reversal, requiring careful attention to conditional direction.
stimulus: If the Byzantine Empire had maintained control of the Silk Road trade routes, its treasury would have remained solvent. Historical records show that the Byzantine treasury did not remain solvent. Therefore, the Byzantine Empire did not maintain control of the Silk Road trade routes.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the printing press had been widely adopted in China during the Song Dynasty, literacy rates would have increased dramatically. Literacy rates did not increase dramatically during the Song Dynasty. Therefore, the printing press was not widely adopted in China during the Song Dynasty.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the Roman aqueducts had been maintained, urban populations would have remained stable. The Roman aqueducts were maintained for several centuries. Therefore, urban populations remained stable during that period.

choices.label: C
choices.text: Had the Mongols continued their westward expansion, Western Europe would have been conquered. Western Europe was not conquered by the Mongols. Therefore, the Mongols did not continue their westward expansion indefinitely.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the Meiji Restoration had failed, Japan would not have industrialized rapidly. Japan did industrialize rapidly. Therefore, the Meiji Restoration did not fail.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If trade networks had flourished in medieval Europe, cultural exchange would have increased. Trade networks did flourish in medieval Europe during certain periods. Therefore, cultural exchange increased during those periods.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: If A then B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A (modus tollens). Choice A: If printing press adopted then literacy increased; literacy did not increase; ∴ printing press not widely adopted. Exact structural match.
explanations.A: Correct. Modus tollens — denial of consequent yields denial of antecedent.
explanations.B: Trap: modus ponens (if A then B; A; ∴ B). Valid but different form from the stimulus.
explanations.C: Trap: same modus tollens structure — A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A — and appears to match. However, the antecedent ('continued indefinitely') is not the same as the original conditional's antecedent, and the conclusion adds the hedge 'indefinitely,' introducing a strength shift. Choice A remains the cleaner match.
explanations.D: Trap: if ¬A then ¬B; B; ∴ A — this is actually valid (contrapositive of ¬A → ¬B is B → A) but the form differs from the stimulus (the antecedent is negated in the conditional). Surface similarity to modus tollens but structurally distinct.
explanations.E: Trap: modus ponens. Same-domain (medieval Europe) content lure.

difficultyReason: Analogy stimulus (X resembles Y in two relevant respects; Y has property R; ∴ X has R) in arts domain; distractors share surface features of the analogy but differ in the number of shared properties cited or reverse the analogical direction.
stimulus: The newly discovered manuscript shares two key features with authenticated works by the composer: its harmonic language and its instrumentation. Since authenticated works by the composer are known to display a recurring modal cadence pattern, the newly discovered manuscript almost certainly displays a recurring modal cadence pattern as well.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: This fossil shares its skeletal proportions and dental structure with the known species Megalodon. Since Megalodon is known to have been apex predator, this fossil almost certainly belonged to an apex predator as well.

choices.label: B
choices.text: This ceramic vessel resembles ancient Greek amphorae. Since ancient Greek amphorae were used to store olive oil, this vessel was probably used to store olive oil.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The newly identified plant specimen has unusual leaf geometry. Other plants with unusual leaf geometry tend to thrive in arid environments. Therefore, this specimen probably thrives in arid environments.

choices.label: D
choices.text: Authenticated works by this sculptor show a preference for marble. Since the newly discovered statue is made of marble, it was almost certainly created by this sculptor.

choices.label: E
choices.text: This symphony shares its key signature and tempo markings with works by Beethoven. Beethoven's works are widely performed today. Therefore, this symphony is widely performed today.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: X shares two specific properties with Y; Y is known to have R; ∴ X almost certainly has R. Choice A: fossil shares two properties (skeletal proportions and dental structure) with Megalodon; Megalodon has R (apex predator); ∴ fossil almost certainly has R. Exact match in analogy structure, property count, and conclusion strength.
explanations.A: Correct. Two shared properties cited, known property of the analog transferred to the subject, 'almost certainly' conclusion strength matches.
explanations.B: Trap: only one shared property (resembles amphorae), not two — premise count mismatch. Also weakens analogy.
explanations.C: Trap: one shared property (leaf geometry) cited; the analog is a category ('other plants'), not a specific named entity. Structure is closer to universal-to-particular than analogy.
explanations.D: Trap: affirms the consequent — Y (authenticated sculptor) has property B (marble); X has B; ∴ X is Y. Inverts the analogical direction.
explanations.E: Trap: two shared properties cited, matching the stimulus premise count, but the transferred property (widely performed) is incidental rather than intrinsic to the shared features — and the conclusion lacks 'almost certainly,' introducing a strength shift.

difficultyReason: Universal-to-particular with a negative universal ('No A is B; x is A; ∴ x is not B') in policy domain; distractors flip the universal to affirmative or use 'some,' requiring attention to quantifier polarity.
stimulus: No policy that relies exclusively on voluntary compliance has ever succeeded in reducing industrial pollution. The proposed carbon-offset scheme relies exclusively on voluntary compliance. Therefore, the proposed carbon-offset scheme will not succeed in reducing industrial pollution.
questionStem: Which one of the following arguments is most similar in its reasoning to the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: No antibiotic that targets only gram-positive bacteria is effective against tuberculosis. Streptomycin targets only gram-positive bacteria. Therefore, streptomycin is not effective against tuberculosis.

choices.label: B
choices.text: Some regulations that rely on voluntary compliance have failed to reduce emissions. This regulation relies on voluntary compliance. Therefore, this regulation will probably fail to reduce emissions.

choices.label: C
choices.text: All renewable-energy mandates require government subsidies. The wind-power initiative requires government subsidies. Therefore, the wind-power initiative is a renewable-energy mandate.

choices.label: D
choices.text: No tax incentive has ever eliminated a harmful industry practice. Corporate tax credits are a form of tax incentive. Therefore, corporate tax credits will not eliminate harmful industry practices.

choices.label: E
choices.text: Voluntary compliance schemes rarely achieve full industry participation. The proposed scheme relies on voluntary compliance. Therefore, the proposed scheme will probably not achieve full industry participation.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: No A is B; x is A; ∴ x is not B — universal negative instantiation. Choice A: No antibiotic that targets only gram-positive bacteria is effective against tuberculosis; streptomycin targets only gram-positive bacteria; ∴ streptomycin is not effective. Perfect structural match.
explanations.A: Correct. Universal negative ('No A is B') applied to a particular instance, yielding a certain negative conclusion.
explanations.B: Trap: strength-shift — 'some' replaces the universal negative, and 'probably' replaces the certain conclusion. Quantifier and conclusion strength both differ.
explanations.C: Trap: affirms the consequent (All A → B; x has B; ∴ x is A). Invalid form despite using a universal premise.
explanations.D: Trap: same-domain (policy/voluntary compliance) content lure. The structure matches at first glance, but the subject of the universal premise ('tax incentive') is broader than the particular instance ('corporate tax credits'), making the instantiation imprecise — this is a subtle premise-count mismatch.
explanations.E: Trap: strength-shift — 'rarely' and 'probably' replace the universal negative and certain conclusion.

difficultyReason: Conditional chain in technology domain (A → B; B → C; ¬C; ∴ ¬A) combining a chain with modus tollens; distractors break the chain or apply modus tollens at the wrong node.
stimulus: If the new operating system is deployed company-wide, all legacy software will need to be upgraded. If all legacy software is upgraded, the IT department's budget will be exceeded. The IT department's budget was not exceeded. Therefore, the new operating system was not deployed company-wide.
questionStem: The pattern of reasoning in which one of the following is most parallel to that in the argument above?

choices.label: A
choices.text: If the dam is constructed upstream, the wetlands downstream will be flooded. If the wetlands are flooded, the migratory bird population will collapse. The migratory bird population did not collapse. Therefore, the dam was not constructed upstream.

choices.label: B
choices.text: If the clinical trial succeeds, the drug will receive regulatory approval. If the drug receives regulatory approval, it will be commercially released. The clinical trial succeeded. Therefore, the drug will be commercially released.

choices.label: C
choices.text: If the server farm is expanded, electricity costs will rise. Electricity costs have risen. Therefore, the server farm was expanded.

choices.label: D
choices.text: If the new software is deployed, legacy systems will require upgrades. Legacy systems have not required upgrades. Therefore, the new software was not deployed.

choices.label: E
choices.text: If network bandwidth is increased, data transfer speeds improve. If data transfer speeds improve, user satisfaction rises. Network bandwidth was not increased. Therefore, user satisfaction did not rise.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A → B; B → C; ¬C; ∴ ¬A — a conditional chain with modus tollens applied to the final consequent. Choice A: dam → wetlands flooded; wetlands flooded → bird population collapses; birds did not collapse; ∴ dam not constructed. Exact three-conditional-link structure with modus tollens at the end.
explanations.A: Correct. Conditional chain plus modus tollens on the final consequent — mirrors the stimulus in premise count, chain direction, and conclusion form.
explanations.B: Trap: modus ponens applied to a two-step chain (A → B; B → C; A; ∴ C). Valid but different — the argument runs forward, not backward via modus tollens.
explanations.C: Trap: affirms the consequent (A → B; B; ∴ A). Invalid form, and only one conditional link rather than two.
explanations.D: Trap: valid modus tollens (A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A) but only one conditional link — missing the chained intermediate step. Same-topic (software deployment) content lure.
explanations.E: Trap: denies the antecedent (A → B; B → C; ¬A; ∴ ¬C). Invalid form — denial of the antecedent is a formal fallacy.

difficultyReason: Disjunctive syllogism embedded within a broader argument (three premises total) in the arts/history domain; distractors use the same domain or reduce to a two-premise disjunction without the supplementary premise.
stimulus: The fresco in the chapel was painted either during the early Renaissance or during the High Renaissance. Art historians agree that its technique is inconsistent with the High Renaissance. Moreover, any artwork whose technique is inconsistent with a given period was not created during that period. Therefore, the fresco was painted during the early Renaissance.
questionStem: The reasoning in the argument above is most similar to the reasoning in which one of the following?

choices.label: A
choices.text: The unidentified mineral sample is either feldspar or quartz. Its refractive index is inconsistent with quartz. Any mineral whose refractive index is inconsistent with a given mineral type is not that mineral type. Therefore, the sample is feldspar.

choices.label: B
choices.text: The poem was written either by Keats or by Shelley. Literary scholars believe it was most likely written by Keats. Therefore, the poem was probably written by Keats.

choices.label: C
choices.text: The artifact is either Minoan or Mycenaean in origin. Its decoration is inconsistent with Mycenaean craftsmanship. Therefore, the artifact is Minoan in origin.

choices.label: D
choices.text: The painting was created either before or after the artist's exile. If it was created before the exile, it would display the artist's early palette. The painting does not display the early palette. Therefore, it was created after the exile.

choices.label: E
choices.text: The mural was executed either in fresco or in tempera. Only a master painter could execute a fresco of this scale. This mural was executed by a master painter. Therefore, this mural was executed in fresco.

explanations.correct: Stimulus: A or B; technique inconsistent with B; any technique inconsistent with a period means not created in that period (universal rule); ∴ A. Three premises — disjunction, observational premise, universal rule — before the conclusion. Choice A matches exactly: disjunction (feldspar or quartz), observational premise (refractive index inconsistent with quartz), universal rule (inconsistent refractive index ≠ that mineral); ∴ feldspar.
explanations.A: Correct. Three-premise structure — disjunction plus observational premise plus explicit universal rule — yielding disjunctive syllogism conclusion. All three premises match in form and count.
explanations.B: Trap: 'most likely' introduces probability rather than eliminating a disjunct through a rule; conclusion is 'probably,' shifting modal strength. No universal rule premise.
explanations.C: Trap: only two premises (disjunction and observational claim) — the explicit universal rule is missing, reducing premise count. Surface similarity to the stimulus is high, making this an effective distractor.
explanations.D: Trap: three premises, but the structure is a conditional chain with modus tollens (A → B; ¬B; ∴ ¬A) rather than a disjunctive syllogism with an embedded universal rule.
explanations.E: Trap: affirms one disjunct by establishing a necessary condition and then affirming it — structurally invalid (affirming the consequent within the disjunction resolution). 'Only a master painter could' means master → fresco, not fresco → master.
